scores.angle: COMPOSER-FIRST (proposal A): face type with proboscis folded in, real-animal eye types, face x horn rules shown in the existing adjustments panel, recipe v3, planet code untouched
scores.notes:
Right target: the owner looked at the deployed Creature Lab in composer mode (docs/fauna-modular-preview-2026-10-02.md links ?mode=composer). The eye design is the best of the two: lidded ring patch, raycast placement along a per-face gaze, and a real wet-cornea highlight through per-vertex gloss. Rule tables are concrete.

VERIFIED flaws:
(1) The phase-1 shim builds from a 'legacy build view' with horns replaced. But mesh.ts:362 recomputes traits from graph.recipe, and individual.ts:87 hashes `horns`. So every horn-omitted recipe would get a new speciesKey and re-roll its individual, coat drift and skin stream. That contradicts A's own herd-stability claim.
(2) Removing the encoded `trunk` key forces a frozen V2 key list and a derived-but-not-encoded field. That is avoidable churn.
(3) Pre-extracting skin-core/head-mesh from the 1,342-line mesh.ts is a large no-feature refactor in the critical path.
(4) Five packages with rig.ts, creature-lab-composer.ts and the structure test changing hands between phases.

scores.angle: SHARED-VOCABULARY (proposal B): one pure fauna-face-1 module for composer and planet, a shared 150-triangle eye template, a painted catchlight, and the planet fix in the same round
scores.notes:
Best catch: planet PADDED animals grow forehead horns. VERIFIED at HEAD: creature-model.ts:101 `selected = family ?? inheritedFaunaFamily(genome)`, and the horn reset sits inside `if(family!==undefined)` at :146/:159, while BASE['low-slung'].hornLength = .08 (:44). The fix is digest-safe because creature-model.ts is a SHARED_PRESENTATION_FILE. Keeping the `trunk` key in the encoding (append-only) is also the right call.

Weaknesses:
- It rewrites the planet eye under an exact 500-triangle cap (2x150 + 2x80 + 2x20), with zero slack, and a six-feature contract pinned in 4 tests. That is high risk for a surface the owner did not ask about.
- A painted catchlight does not move when the Lab orbits, and the composer is not digest-gated, so a real specular highlight is affordable there.
- 'trunk always normalizes to none' plus rewriting every r.trunk read is more churn than deriving trunk from the face.
- A shared template forces the composer eye into the planet's projected-disc topology.
- WP0 + WP1 are very large, and WP1 owns mesh.ts, rig.ts and all composer pins at once.

rationale:
Synthesis, checked against the actual repo. HEAD is now c80c8dd, not 9688bc3. The gate added a docs commit and two small commits that touched creature-lab-composer.ts (+10 lines) and fauna-composer-mesh.ts (5 lines). The working tree is clean, and every cited line below was re-read at c80c8dd.

VERIFIED at c80c8dd:
- recipe.ts:19 head enum; :28 `trunk` is a free part; :267-270 are the only two face rules; :334 wild trunk weights [3,1].
- rig.ts:144 HEAD_SCALE is a Record over head, so adding a face value is a tsc error until it is handled. :176-178 cranium ratios; :333 headPitch; :361-373 trunk chain with a root formula fixed for every face.
- mesh.ts:980 nostrils use pal.eye; :985 ears silently dropped for paired/ossicones; :1020 blunt disc uses pal.eye; :1035 mandible compound ellipsoids; :1040-1047 8x4 eye ellipsoid with the cos(a)*side > .75 'glint'; :1050-1083 horns, with the trunk-forehead path at :1058.
- mesh.ts:362 traits = composerIndividualTraits(graph.recipe); individual.ts:31,87 the species key hashes head, horns and trunk; mesh.ts:384-392 skin-ind stream has 12 draws, with the iris shade at u9[11].
- fauna-composer.ts:52 one MeshStandardMaterial (roughness .82).
- creature-lab.ts:144 the composer camera fits the whole envelope only.
- package.json "test" lists every test explicitly, so new tests must be registered there.

Scratch census, using my synthesized rule table (test-results/fauna-face-plan-2026-10-02/judge-rule-counts.mjs):
- Pinned skin-2 texts: 13 of 28 would drift in phase 1 (11 horn, 2 trunk dropped, 1 becomes proboscis).
- Legacy v1 fixture texts: 164 of 420 horn, 78 trunk dropped.
- Wild seeds: 454 of 1000 horn, 199 trunk dropped.
- Coherent species: 4 of 1000 horn.
- Presets: 3 hybrids (shelled-giraffe-bird, trunked-centipede, winged-ape-rhino).

Decisions:
(1) Composer first, because that is what the owner sees. From B I take only the planet PADDED horn fix: one rule plus a mutationLog line in a shared file, no digest re-baseline. Planet eyes are deferred.
(2) Keep the encoded `trunk` key, but derive it: trunk = (head === 'proboscis'). So rig/mesh trunk code keeps working, there is no frozen key removal, and the encoding stays append-only. Append 'proboscis' to head, and append the keys 'eyes' and 'iris' (version bumps to 3).
(3) graph.recipe stays the chosen recipe. Mesh reads composerSkullOf(face) and composerHeadgearBuild(recipe). The species key projects only proboscis -> muzzle, so herds never re-roll except the 78 asserted dropped-trunk links. This fixes A's verified re-roll bug.
(4) No skin-core extraction. Eye geometry is a new pure module that returns head-local patch data, and mesh.ts emits it. mesh.ts is therefore owned serially: WP1 (shims), then WP4 (eyes), then WP5 (head geometry).
(5) Real per-vertex gloss on the composer material through one onBeforeCompile patch. That gives a view-dependent corneal highlight with one material and one draw call. The composer is outside the life-cpu digest gate.
(6) Generators obey the rules after drawing (no new draws). Hand-made and legacy links keep their choices and get disclosures.

Owner's three asks map as follows: trunk -> face type (WP1 contract, WP5 geometry); eye types (WP1 vocabulary, WP4 geometry, WP6 UI); horns that make no sense (WP1 rules, generators and disclosure; WP5 casque and ears; WP3 planet).

plan.thesis:
VERIFIED at HEAD c80c8dd. The composer already treats `head` as a face type (fauna-composer-recipe.ts:19). The owner's three complaints come from three verified gaps:

(a) The trunk is an independent part (recipe.ts:28). Its root is the same rig position for every face (rig.ts:365), so on beaks it floats in front of the face. On muzzles it is bolted onto a full horse-length snout.

(b) Eyes are untyped 8x4 near-black ellipsoids (mesh.ts:1040-1047). Their only highlight sits on the medial side, inside the skull. Nostrils and the worm mouth reuse the eye colour (mesh.ts:980, :1020).

(c) No face x horn rule exists. composerConstraints (recipe.ts:252-290) has 2 face rules. 454 of 1000 wild seeds build horns on unsuitable faces. mesh.ts:985 silently deletes ears under paired horns or ossicones. On the planet, PADDED animals grow horns because the family horn reset only runs on the explicit-family path (creature-model.ts:101, :146-159).

The increment, in four steps:
(1) A pure module, src/fauna-composer-face.ts, holds the vocabulary, rule tables, eye auto-resolution, migration and species-key projection. Recipe v3 appends head 'proboscis' and the keys eyes and iris, and makes `trunk` a derived field (trunk = face is proboscis). The generators obey the rules after drawing, with no new draws. Every horn that is not built as chosen yields one 'Horns' constraint. Legacy links migrate with a line under 'This link was adjusted'.
(2) New eyes: a lidded concentric-ring patch with an anisotropic pupil, an iris and limbus, a lid and orbit blend. It is placed by raycasting the built skull along a per-face gaze direction, with a per-vertex gloss for a real corneal highlight. Compound domes on arthropods, eyespots on worms.
(3) Head geometry: a real proboscis face (shortened muzzle flowing into the trunk, mouth below, flap ears, nostrils at the trunk tip), a beak casque, a seated thick crest, ears kept behind horn bases, and a flat face whose eyes are not covered by the brow.
(4) Creature Lab: Face, Eyes and Iris selectors; per-option 'not built on this face' hints; a resolved 'Automatic (...)' label; a 'Head and face' frame in composer mode.

Determinism: no frozen stream gets a new draw. Herds stay stable except the asserted dropped-trunk links.

faceTypes.description:
Mammal muzzle (horse, deer, bovid, giraffe, rhino, dog). The existing value.
- Eyes: auto gives horizontal-bar on grazers (feet 'hoof' or legs 'unguligrade'), round on 'pillar' legs, a vertical slit on paw/claw/pad carnivores with bodyLength < 0.9, and round on larger ones.
- After WP5, ears are kept, placed below and behind the horn bases, instead of being deleted (mesh.ts:985).
- After WP4, nostrils get their own 'nose' colour (skin x .22) instead of pal.eye; WP5 makes them protrude past the end cap.
- Iris: dark-brown or brown, from a hash of colorSeed.
allowedHeadgear: none
nasal (rhino keratin horn on the nose ridge; built)
paired (bovid horns; built, roots moved forward onto the frontal bone in WP5)
ossicones (giraffe; built)
crest -> NOT built: 'Not built: mammal skulls carry no bony crest. Choose Paired horns or Ossicones.'
bodyPlans: coherent archetypes: ungulate-grazer, giraffid, cursorial-carnivore, pachyderm without trunk

faceTypes.description:
NEW appended head value: the trunk face (elephant, tapir). A trunk is a nose; the mouth stays below it.
- Recipe: trunk becomes the derived value 'trunk', and trunkLength is relabelled 'Proboscis length'.
- WP1 (shim): composerSkullOf('proboscis') = 'muzzle', so it builds bit-identical to legacy muzzle+trunk, apart from the horn rules.
- WP5 (real face): HEAD_SCALE 1.05, cranium height ratio .40, snout = 0.4 x the muzzle snout.
  - The trunk root comes from composerFaceTip(), shared by rig and mesh. The first trunk ring is the open muzzle's last ring (the neck-to-head blend technique), so there is no collar.
  - Tip ellipsoid [0.9,1,1]r0 instead of [0.9,1.12,1.12]r0, so there is no lip step.
  - A lower lip/mouth part under the root, two nostril pits on the trunk tip, and broad lateral flap ears.
- Eyes: small (k = .07), high and lateral (gaze 70 degrees from the midline). Auto gives round, dark brown.
- The rig keeps the 6-bone trunk chain, so bone counts equal legacy muzzle+trunk.
allowedHeadgear: none
paired (saiga-like; built)
nasal -> NOT built: 'Not built: a trunk face has no nose bones to carry a horn.' (replaces the forehead relocation at recipe.ts:269 / mesh.ts:1058)
ossicones -> NOT built: 'Not built: ossicones grow only on giraffe-like muzzles.'
crest -> NOT built: 'Not built: mammal skulls carry no bony crest.'
bodyPlans: coherent archetype: pachyderm (a drawn trunk on a muzzle becomes proboscis after the draw)

faceTypes.description:
Toothed reptile or theropod snout (crocodile, monitor lizard, theropod).
- Eyes: auto gives a vertical slit on sprawled or limbless layouts and round on biped or quadruped. Iris gold, amber, copper or green-yellow by hash.
- WP5 rebuilds the crest as a seated lofted fin at least 0.18 cW thick, replacing the 0.07 cW floating slab (mesh.ts:1080).
allowedHeadgear: none
nasal (ceratopsian or rhino-iguana; built)
paired (brow horns; built)
crest (bony crest; built)
ossicones -> built as paired: 'Built as brow horns: ossicones grow only on giraffe-like muzzles.'
bodyPlans: coherent archetypes: theropod, sprawler-lizard (mandibles off many-legged bodies already become jaws, species.ts:180)

faceTypes.description:
Bird or turtle keratin bill.
- Eyes: auto gives round. They are large (k .16, down from .17), lateral (gaze 75 degrees) and set into the skull by the raycast placement, instead of sticking out at 0.86 cW.
- Iris: yellow, orange, red or dark on bipeds; dark-brown or green on sprawled layouts (turtles). Juvenile iris (maturity < .75) is blended toward dark.
- The only headgear is a keratin casque on the culmen (WP5).
allowedHeadgear: none
crest -> built as casque (WP5 geometry; no constraint, the UI labels the option 'Crest or casque')
nasal -> built as crest/casque: 'Built as a casque: a beak carries a casque, not a nose horn.'
paired -> NOT built: 'Not built: birds and turtles never grow horns; only a casque (Crest).'
ossicones -> NOT built (same text)

faceTypes.description:
Primate face.
- Eyes: forward (gaze 15 degrees from the midline), round, dark-brown or brown iris, no white sclera.
- WP5 raises the brow ellipsoid (centre y .22 cH to .30 cH, half-height .12 cH to .09 cH), so it no longer covers the upper eye. The eyes currently read as closed slits; compare mesh.ts:1011 with :1045. WP5 also adds a nose bump and a mouth line on the lower-face loft.
- No headgear.
allowedHeadgear: none
nasal/paired/ossicones/crest -> NOT built: 'Not built: primate faces carry no horns.'

faceTypes.description:
Worm head cap.
- Eyes: two pigment eyespots (8-segment flush dark discs on the upper front of the cap).
- WP4: the frontal mouth disc gets its own 'mouth' colour (skin darkened .3) instead of pal.eye.
- WP5: the disc is seated on the cap; today it floats about 0.12 cW ahead (mesh.ts:1020).
- No headgear.
allowedHeadgear: none
any horn -> NOT built: 'Not built: a worm head has no skull to carry horns.'

faceTypes.description: Arthropod head capsule. Compound-eye domes with a dark pseudopupil and facet shading replace the ellipsoids at mesh.ts:1035. Antennae and mandibles are unchanged. No horns.
allowedHeadgear: none
any horn -> NOT built: 'Not built: arthropod heads carry no bony horns.'

eyeTypes.description:
Default for every migrated and generated recipe.

resolveComposerEyes(recipe) in fauna-composer-face.ts is a pure function. The pupil type depends only on face, layout, legs, feet and bodyLength, never on colorSeed, because coat and colour must not change geometry (structure-independent.test.mjs:64-65). The iris band comes from composerHash(`face-eye-v1/${colorSeed}/${face}`) over the face's allowed bands. No stream draws, so it is shared across a herd.

Auto table:
- mandibles -> compound
- blunt -> eyespot
- beak -> round
- flat-face -> round
- proboscis -> round
- muzzle: hoof feet or unguligrade legs -> horizontal; pillar legs -> round; otherwise bodyLength < 0.9 -> vertical-slit, else round
- jaws: sprawled or limbless -> vertical-slit; otherwise round
eyeTypes.geometryAndShading:
Resolves to one of the types below.

IRIS vocabulary (append-only), with a starting linear-RGB table in fauna-composer-face.ts that WP4 may tune and then pin:
- dark-brown [.035,.018,.008]
- brown [.09,.045,.015]
- amber [.40,.20,.03]
- gold [.55,.38,.06]
- yellow [.70,.55,.05]
- orange [.70,.25,.03]
- red [.50,.04,.02]
- green [.18,.28,.06]
- pale [.55,.55,.50]

The iris is multiplied by the existing eyeMul (u9[11], mesh.ts:390). Contrast floor: iris luminance >= 1.8 x the lid-rim luminance, so eyes stay visible on ink and slate coats.

eyeTypes.description: Circular pupil. Found in tall or active predators, diurnal predators, nearly all birds, primates, theropods and elephants (Banks et al. 2015; research-sourced, not re-verified here).
Horizontal bar pupil, as in goats, sheep, horses and deer: lateral-eyed grazing prey.
eyeTypes.geometryAndShading:
Same patch. R1/R2 use a superellipse (n = 4) with rx .55 and ry .16.

The bar axis is the head-forward direction projected onto the eye plane, blended 0.7 toward the world-horizontal projection. That counter-rolls the rest head pitch, which is -0.3 rad on most quadrupeds (rig.ts:333). Iris dark-brown or brown.

eyeTypes.description: Vertical slit pupil, as in cats, foxes, crocodiles and geckos: short ambush predators.
eyeTypes.geometryAndShading:
Same patch. R1/R2 use rx .08 and ry .46, with lens-pointed ends (half-width x |cos|^0.6). The iris fills .95 of the opening.

Iris amber or gold on carnivores; gold, copper or green on reptiles.

eyeTypes.description:
Arthropod compound eye. Only built on mandibles faces.

On a vertebrate face it is built as the auto type, with the constraint 'Eyes: built as <auto>: compound eyes belong to arthropod heads.' A vertebrate pupil chosen on mandibles is built as compound, with the constraint 'Built as compound: arthropod heads have compound eyes.'
eyeTypes.geometryAndShading:
A dome with 12 radial segments x 5 stations, at most 120 triangles per eye, placed where mesh.ts:1035 is now.
- Facet checker: vertex colour +/-8% between alternating rings and segments.
- A 3-vertex dark pseudopupil at the gaze apex.
- Gloss .35.

eyeTypes.description:
Worm pigment-cup eyespots. Only built on blunt faces.

Elsewhere they are built as the auto type, with a disclosure. Any iris choice on a compound or eyespot face gives 'Iris colour has no effect: compound eyes and eyespots have no iris.'
eyeTypes.geometryAndShading: Two flush dark discs of 8 segments (8 triangles each) on the upper front of the cap, lifted .002 H. Gloss 0.
